domain: Gives item_id to whichever party member PartyInventory_Add (the Func_08077030 far-call veneer onto games/gs1/src/inventory/add_to_party.c's real body at 0x08078618) can hold it for. If every member's bag is full (-1 returned), opens a message/window sequence (UiText_DrawQuantity/UiText_DrawMessage veneers at Func_08015120/Func_08015040) telling the player the item was obtained but bags are full, then loops Shop_SelectPartyMemberItem (the Func_080b0058 veneer onto the still-unadopted, source-paths-named-only 0x080b3444) so the player can either pick a member+slot to discard or cancel: picking a key-flagged item (Item_GetData(item_id)->flags & 8, via the already-declared item.h prototype) re-prompts in place; cancelling asks a yes/no confirm through sibling owner Func_08091d84 (games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/runtime/runtime_owner_190.c) and, on a real cancel, restores the transient field and returns -1 with Item_AdjustCounter bumped by 1 (the Func_08077240 veneer onto games/gs1/src/item/adjust_counter.c's real body at 0x08078ad0). A confirmed discard target instead drains the chosen slot's full stack via Inventory_GetQuantity/Inventory_Discard-shaped veneers (Func_08077020, Func_080772b0, both far-call variants of the already-adopted games/gs1/src/inventory/get_quantity.c and games/gs1/src/inventory/discard.c bodies) after touching the owner's state once through the Func_08077008 veneer (games/gs1/include/owner_state.h's already-declared OwnerState_GetFar/struct OwnerInventoryState*), then retries PartyInventory_Add. Either success path plays the pickup cue (Audio_PlayCue/Func_080f9010, 83) and prints either the generic 'you got the item' message (0x96a) or, when the receiving owner differs from games/gs1/include/party_state.h's Data_02000240.current_owner, a named-recipient variant (0x96b). Throughout, a transient s16 field at offset 472 (236 halfwords) of the runtime block behind Data_03001ebc is saved on entry and restored on every exit.

This is the genuine evidence trail for the whole function, not a template guess.

0x03001ebc dereferences to a runtime-block pointer (games/gs1/include/battle_effect_runtime.h's struct BattleRuntime, whose unknown_1d0[0x0a] padding covers offset 0x1d8=472 -- not renamed here, header left untouched to avoid disturbing its many other callers) and 0x02000240+500(0x1f4) is exactly games/gs1/include/party_state.h's struct PartyState.current_owner -- both confirmed by matching field width/offset against already-committed headers, not guessed.

Sibling Func_08091d84 (games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/runtime/runtime_owner_190.c) is s32(s32), a thin wrapper over Func_08015390(value,0,0,0); used here as a yes/no confirm gate matching the surrounding message flow.

m2c workbench (cargo run --manifest-path tools/compiler/Cargo.toml -- workbench games/gs1/recon/en/main/08091a58.c) ran cleanly once main:08091a58 was given the {"name":"PartyInventory_GiveItem"} registration this session added to source-paths.json (workbench requires a registered owner symbol; the matching '.global PartyInventory_GiveItem' alias label was added to games/gs1/asm/08091a58.s immediately above the existing Func_08091a58 label, verified present in the retained assembly's own exports). m2c's --valid-syntax draft against the real agscc type context independently reproduced the same control-flow shape, message IDs (0x96a/0x96b/0x977/0x978/0x979/0x97a/0x97c), and both global accesses this hand trace already had, which is strong corroboration rather than a separate source of evidence.

Iterated three source-shape variants via workbench objdiff: (1) a first draft using early 'return' statements inside a for(;;) loop scored 56.5% (candidate 415, later variants smaller); (2) caching Data_03001ebc's dereferenced value in a named 'base' pointer (avoiding 2 of 3 restore sites re-dereferencing the global from scratch) raised it to 61.0%; (3) caching the full field address ('s16 *fld = (s16*)((u8*)Data_03001ebc+472)') instead of the base pointer alone raised it further to 61.7% (candidate=400, differing_halfwords=214, wrong_instructions=137) -- the version kept.

Residual is register-role/tail-merge allocation, not a remaining algorithm or control-flow gap: the reference caches the runtime-block pointer permanently in fp and spills the saved field value to the stack for two of its three restore sites while keeping it register-resident for the third (the path reachable without entering the retry loop), producing three textually-distinct-but-logically-identical restore sequences that GCC never merges. This candidate's allocator instead keeps the saved value uniformly in fp across all three call sites, so two of the three restore sequences become byte-identical and GCC 2.96 tail-merges them into one shared block, which in turn forces an extra unconditional branch (the immediate-success path can no longer fall straight through into its own inline restore). This is the same qty_compare/local-alloc tie-break-by-RTL-discovery-order residual class already traced to alchemy-gcc/agscc/gcc/local-alloc.c and documented as architecturally uncontrollable by plain source reordering in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080a8c2c.json (confirmed there across four independent owners this session); this owner's declaration-order and statement-order variants (swapping saved/fld computation order, narrowing saved to s16) all measured zero effect on the split, consistent with that finding. No register hint, asm(), or PERM_GENERAL forcing was used.
